stops.note: the verb 'to break', applied to a road broken or cut through a forest
from rupta (via), literally '(a road) broken open'
route plus the suffix -ine, coined for a habitual, well-worn course of action
stops.meaning: a customary, mechanical course of action

stops.note: adopted for any fixed, habitual way of doing things
stops.meaning: a fixed, regular way of doing things
